page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2863.28 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2458.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11475.63 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6895.0. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 565.78 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are weak to poor, measuring 36.05 GB/sec and 13.63 GB/sec respectively.

This server configuration is suitable for workloads such as database operations, static web serving, and text processing, where its local NVMe SSD and strong single-core performance can be leveraged. It also supports moderate software compilation and small-model LLM inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a bundled local NVMe SSD provides a balanced resource density for general-purpose computing, though memory-intensive applications requiring high uncached write bandwidth may face performance bottlenecks.
